newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Ping'an Insurance '96 revenue doubles.
newsitem.headline: China's Ping'an Insurance '96 revenue doubles.

text.p: Shenzhen-based Ping'an Insurance Co of China Ltd said on Tuesday its revenue for 1996 reached 10.5 billion yuan ($1.27 billion), more than doubling its 5.0 billion yuan 1995 revenue.

Ping'an's revenue has doubled each year since 1993, a company spokesman told the Hong Kong-based China Securities Bulletin on Tuesday. He added he expected growth to slow in 1997 given the company's size.

Of the 10.5 billion yuan in revenue, 3.5 billion came from the property sector and 7.0 billion from life insurance premiums, the spokesman said. "The general insurance market trend is good ... it is set for gains," he said.
But state media have said cut-throat competition and poor management have eaten into insurance profit in Shenzhen, the southern city which borders Hong Kong.
Nationwide floods that hit China last summer cost the company a great deal, the spokesman said but gave no details.
The company paid a total of 2.0 billion yuan in 1996 for damage insurance.

Ping'an had signed 25 contracts worth more than 1.0 billion yuan each last year, including Ling'ao nuclear power plant in southern Guangdong province and a 60-floor office building in Shenzhen, the spokesman said.
The company's total assets reached 15 billion yuan at the end of 1996, he added.
